title: Filteredness of the pair henselization category
statement: For a commutative ring B and ideal J, let C be the full category of ring maps B to D with Spec(D) to Spec(B) etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and the canonical map B/J to D/JD bijective, with all B-algebra maps as morphisms. Then C is filtered: it is nonempty, any two objects admit a common successor, and every pair of parallel maps is coequalized.

proof.text: *(1) Nonempty; two objects map to a common one.* $B$ itself (identity) is an object: $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the identity, an open immersion, hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), and $\bar B\to B/J$ is the identity. Let $C,C'$ be objects and $C''=C\otimes_BC'$. $\operatorname{Spec}C''\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is etale as a base change of $B\to C'$ along $B\to C$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change], hence $\operatorname{Spec}C''\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is etale (composition, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2)). Reduction modulo $J$: by associativity and commutativity of tensor products, $C''/JC''=C''\otimes_B\bar B\cong(C\otimes_B\bar B)\otimes_{\bar B}(C'\otimes_B\bar B)=(C/JC)\otimes_{\bar B}(C'/JC')$, and under this identification the map $\bar B\to C''/JC''$ is the tensor product of the isomorphisms $\bar B\to C/JC$, $\bar B\to C'/JC'$ over $\bar B$, so it is the isomorphism $\bar B\cong\bar B\otimes_{\bar B}\bar B\to(C/JC)\otimes_{\bar B}(C'/JC')$. So $C''$ is an object, and the coprojections $C\to C''$, $C'\to C''$ are $B$-algebra maps, i.e. morphisms of $\mathcal C$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization): 'It is nonempty because $\mathrm{id}:A\to A$ is an object. If $B$ and $B'$ are two objects of $\mathcal C$, then $B''=B\otimes_AB'$ is an object of $\mathcal C$ (use Algebra, Lemma 00U2)'; the reduction mod $J$ is written out by the agent

proof.text: *(1) Parallel morphisms are coequalized; $\mathcal C$ is filtered.* Let $f,g:C\to C'$ be morphisms of $\mathcal C$. Put $E=C'\otimes_{f,C,g}C'$ and $D=E\otimes_{C'\otimes_BC'}C'$, formed with the natural surjection $C'\otimes_BC'\to E$ and the multiplication $\mu:C'\otimes_BC'\to C'$. Etaleness over $B$: $f$ is etale (step 1), so the right factor map $C'\to E$, the base change of $f$ along $g$, is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] and $E$ is etale over $B$ (composition); $C'\otimes_BC'$ is etale over $B$ (step 3), so $\mu$ is etale (a map between $B$-algebras etale over $B$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (3)), so $E\to D$, its base change, is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] and $D$ is etale over $B$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2). Reduction modulo $J$ (written out by the agent; Stacks only states etaleness): base change $-\otimes_B\bar B$ commutes with the tensor products, so $D/JD\cong(\bar C'\otimes_{\bar f,\bar C,\bar g}\bar C')\otimes_{\bar C'\otimes_{\bar B}\bar C'}\bar C'$ with $\bar C=C/JC$, $\bar C'=C'/JC'$; the structure maps $\bar B\to\bar C$, $\bar B\to\bar C'$ are isomorphisms through which $\bar f,\bar g$ become $\mathrm{id}_{\bar B}$ ($B$-algebra maps $\bar B\to\bar B$, step 1), so $D/JD\cong(\bar B\otimes_{\bar B}\bar B)\otimes_{\bar B\otimes_{\bar B}\bar B}\bar B\cong\bar B$ and the structure map $\bar B\to D/JD$ is this isomorphism. So $D$ is an object. Let $c:C'\to D$ be the right-most factor map $a\mapsto1\otimes a$, a $B$-algebra map, hence a morphism. In $D$, $c(a)$ equals the image of $a\otimes1$ and of $1\otimes a\in C'\otimes_BC'$ (both map to $a$ under $\mu$); since $f(x)\otimes1=1\otimes g(x)$ in $E$ for $x\in C$, $c(f(x))=c(g(x))$, i.e. $c\circ f=c\circ g$. With step 3, $\mathcal C$ is filtered (Stacks 'directed', Categories Definition Tag 002V).

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization): 'Suppose that $f,g:B\to B'$ are two maps between objects of $\mathcal C$. Then a coequalizer is $(B'\otimes_{f,B,g}B')\otimes_{(B'\otimes_AB')}B'$ which is etale over $A$ by Algebra, Lemmas 00U2 and 00U7'

mathlib_searches.query: A filtered colimit of etale ring algebras inducing the same quotient by an ideal is a henselian pair

lean.statement: theorem pair_henselization_filtered (B : Type u) [CommRing B] (J : Ideal B) : IsFiltered (ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun C : Under (CommRingCat.of B) ↦ AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map C.hom) ∧ Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (J.map C.hom.hom) C.hom.hom (Ideal.le_comap_map))))
